patch_description:
Restructures the two-parameter shared-entangler ansatz by interleaving the
global RZ rotation layer between entangling shells (rather than applying it
once up front) and adding a final global RY "output mixer" layer that reuses
the existing theta_ry parameter (no new trainable parameter). Concretely, the
per-block sequence becomes: RY(all) -> CRZ shell-1(dist 1) -> RZ(all) -> CRZ
shell-2(dist 2) -> CRZ shell-3(dist 4) -> RY(all). This keeps the proven
2-distinct-parameter economy (4 total trainable scalars) while:
 (1) letting the RZ rotation act as a genuine intermediate layer between two
     groups of entangling gates instead of purely a pre-entanglement bias,
     which changes how gradients flow through the tied 3x repeated block and
     should reduce the chance of the optimizer settling into a shallow basin
     that only separates average-difficulty samples;
 (2) adding a final local RY realignment step (reusing theta_ry, so zero
     extra parameters) immediately before the fixed two-qubit readout
     observable is measured, giving the model one more chance to rotate
     qubit Bloch vectors into the observable's eigenbasis and improve worst-
     group margin without inflating parameter count.
No new gate types, no new distinct parameter names, and connectivity shells
are otherwise unchanged (rings at graph distances 1, 2, and 4 on the 8-qubit
cycle), preserving the well-tested, symmetry-respecting entangling structure
of the best prior candidate (score 0.61) while probing a structural change
that prior recommendations flagged as promising.
